Matalas ba ang paningin ng baboy?

Hindi pala! Hindi gaanong matalas ang paningin ng baboy, pero napakahusay ng kanilang pang-amoy — ginagamit nila ito para humanap ng pagkain at makaramdam ng panganib.

Dili diay! Dili kaayo hait ang panan-aw sa baboy, apan maayo kaayo ang ilang panimaho — gigamit nila kini aron mangita og pagkaon ug makamatngon sa kakuyaw.

Oo! Ang nautilus usa ka cephalopod usab, busa paryente kini sa kugita ug nokus bisan adunay gahi nga kabhang.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a fact about a nautilus but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups required by G5-L-4.

copy.en:
How many tentacles does a nautilus have?

Unlike an octopus with just eight arms, a nautilus has around ninety tentacles — and none of them have suckers!
copy.tl:
Ilang galamay meron ang nautilus?

Hindi tulad ng pugita na may walong galamay lang, ang nautilus ay may mga siyamnapung galamay na walang sipsip!
copy.bis:
Pila ka galamay ang naa sa nautilus?

Dili sama sa kugita nga adunay walo ra ka bukton, ang nautilus adunay mga kasiyaman ka galamay nga walay sipsip!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: using gas inside its shell
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the nautilus's daily vertical movement and feeding behavior, but does not describe any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or food gathering. The mention of gas inside the shell is internal, not an outer body part. Thus it only shares the general topic of animal movement/feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rises to shallow water to feed, then sinks back into the deep by day to hide
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a daily behavioral pattern of the nautilus, not a change that better suits its environment over time (adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage). It does not describe how the animal has changed to suit its environment; it only describes a current behavior. Thus it is related to animal-environment interaction but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: At night, the nautilus rises to shallow water to feed, then sinks back into the deep by day to hide, using gas inside its shell.
copy.tl: Tuwing gabi, umaakyat ang nautilus sa mababaw na tubig para kumain, pagkatapos ay lumulubog ito pabalik sa malalim tuwing araw para magtago, gamit ang gas sa loob ng shell nito.
copy.bis: Kada gabii, mosaka ang nautilus sa mabaw nga tubig aron mokaon, dayon molugdang balik sa lawom kada adlaw aron motago, gamit ang gas sulod sa iyang kabibe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every wave needs a push to start!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that waves need a source to start, mentioning sound and a rope wave as examples. It does not identify differences or similarities between longitudinal and transverse waves, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: Every wave needs a push to start! Sound needs something vibrating, and a rope wave needs a hand giving it a shake!
copy.tl: Bawat alon kailangan ng simula! Ang tunog kailangan ng nanginginig na bagay, at ang alon sa lubid kailangan ng kamay na kumikilos!
copy.bis: Matag balod nanginahanglan ug pagsugod! Ang tingog nanginahanglan ug butang nga nagkurog, ug ang balod sa pisi nanginahanglan ug kamot nga naglihok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny filtering units that remove waste from your blood and make urine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the nephron as a kidney filtering unit, which is background about the excretory system. However, the competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). The card uses no such representation and does not explain system interactions, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Each kidney has about one million nephrons — tiny filtering units that remove waste from your blood and make urine.
copy.tl: Ang bawat kidney ay may halos isang milyong nephron — maliliit na yunit ng pagsasala na nag-aalis ng basura mula sa dugo at gumagawa ng ihi.
copy.bis: Ang matag kidney adunay mga usa ka milyon nga nephron — gagmayng unit sa pagsala nga nagtangtang sa basura gikan sa dugo ug nagpatubo og ihi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune's surface gravity is about 11 m/s²
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a gravity value for Neptune, but the competency requires identifying gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth. The card does not address the non-contact nature of gravity or Earth-specific behavior.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Neptune's surface gravity is about 11 m/s²
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a surface gravity value but does not describe effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It is only tangentially related to gravity.

copy.en:
What is the surface gravity on Neptune?

Neptune's surface gravity is about 11 m/s², making it slightly stronger than Earth's 9.8 m/s²!
copy.tl:
Ano ang surface gravity sa Neptune?

Ang surface gravity ng Neptune ay mga 11 m/s², na bahagyang mas malakas kaysa 9.8 m/s² ng Daigdig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang surface gravity sa Neptune?

Ang surface gravity sa Neptune mga 11 m/s², nga gamay nga mas kusog kaysa 9.8 m/s² sa Yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Urbain Le Verrier predicted Neptune's exact location using mathematics
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a historical anecdote about how Neptune was discovered through mathematical prediction. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features or composition. It only mentions Neptune as a planet, which is related vocabulary but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How did scientists find Neptune before they even saw it?

Urbain Le Verrier predicted Neptune's exact location using mathematics before the planet was ever actually seen!
copy.tl:
Paano nahulaan ang lokasyon ng Neptune bago ito makita?

Hinulaan ni Urbain Le Verrier ang lugar ng Neptune gamit ang matematika bago pa ito nakita!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtagna ang nahimutangan sa Neptune sa wala pa kini makita?

Gitagna ni Urbain Le Verrier ang nahimutangan sa Neptune gamit ang matematika sa wala pa kini makita!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds build cups, burrows, mounds, or even woven bags, depending on their kind
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes variation in nest shapes among bird species, not how animals have changed to better suit their environment (e.g., mimicry or camouflage). It does not support the adaptation concept of G5-L-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds build cups, burrows, mounds, or even woven bags, depending on their kind
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about nest-building behavior and species differences, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support G3-L-3.

copy.en: Not all bird nests look the same — birds build cups, burrows, mounds, or even woven bags, depending on their kind!
copy.tl: Hindi magkakapareho ang pugad ng mga ibon — gumagawa sila ng tasa, lungga, bunton, o kaya'y hinabing bag, depende sa uri nila!
copy.bis: Dili managsama ang salag sa mga langgam — naghimo sila og tasa, langub, tumpok, o gihabi nga bag, depende sa ilang klase!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A neuron is a nerve cell — the basic building block of your whole nervous system!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a neuron as a nerve cell and building block of the nervous system, but does not address the concept of unicellular vs. multicellular organisms, which is the core of G7-L-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A neuron is a nerve cell — the basic building block of your whole nervous system!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a cell as a building block but does not use a labelled diagram to describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere, as required by G7-L-8.

copy.en:
What is a neuron?

A neuron is a nerve cell — the basic building block of your whole nervous system!
copy.tl:
Ano ang neuron?

Ang neuron ay isang selula ng nerbiyos — ang pangunahing yunit ng buong sistemang nerbiyos mo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang neuron?

Ang neuron usa ka selula sa nerbiyos — ang sukaranang yunit sa imong tibuok sistema sa nerbiyos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an antacid like Kremil-S acts as a mild base to neutralize the extra acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe important types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions neutralization, which is an acid-base reaction, but does not describe any of the required reaction types (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement). It provides no instructional support for classifying or describing these reaction types.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an antacid like Kremil-S acts as a mild base to neutralize the extra acid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of neutralization in the body, but the competency focuses on important reaction types such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration and their environmental impacts. Neutralization of stomach acid is not one of the listed reaction types, and the card does not explain how a reaction type relates to or impacts the natural or built environment.

copy.en: When your stomach hurts from hyperacidity, an antacid like Kremil-S acts as a mild base to neutralize the extra acid, easing the pain. That is neutralization inside your body!
copy.tl: Kapag sumakit ang tiyan dahil sa hyperacidity, ang antacid gaya ng Kremil-S ay banayad na base na nag-neutralize sa sobrang acid, nababawasan ang kirot. Ito ay neutralization sa loob ng katawan!
copy.bis: Kung sakit ang tiyan tungod sa hyperacidity, ang antacid sama sa Kremil-S usa ka hinay nga base nga mo-neutralize sa sobra nga acid, mokunhod ang kasakit. Kini neutralization sulod sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To fully neutralize a strong acid, you need enough base to match all the H+ it releases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe important types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses acid-base neutralization but does not describe or classify the important types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement). Neutralization is a double-replacement reaction, but the card never names or explains reaction types, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To fully neutralize a strong acid, you need enough base to match all the H+ it releases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that chemical equations demonstrate a rearrangement of atoms but the total mass of the system remains the same during a chemical reaction
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the amount of base needed for neutralization, which relates to stoichiometry, but it does not explain chemical equations, rearrangement of atoms, or conservation of mass. No equation or mass-balance concept is presented, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To fully neutralize a strong acid, you need enough base to match all the H+ it releases.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that scientists: a. use chemical equations to describe chemical reactions, and b. write equations in word form and using formula for common chemical reactions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the concept of neutralization but does not use or write chemical equations in word or formula form, nor does it recognize how scientists use equations to describe reactions. It is only tangentially related to chemical equations.

copy.en:
Does a strong acid need a lot of base to neutralize?

Yes, the amount matters! To fully neutralize a strong acid, you need enough base to match all the H+ it releases. If there's not enough base, some acid is left over.
copy.tl:
Kailangan ba ng maraming base para sa malakas na asido?

Oo, mahalaga ang dami! Para tuluyang ma-neutralize, kailangan mo ng sapat na base na tutugma sa lahat ng H+ nito. Kung kulang, may matitirang asido pa rin.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan ba og daghan nga base para sa kusgan nga asido?

Oo, importante ang gidaghanon! Aron bug-os nga ma-neutralize, kinahanglan nimo og igo nga base nga motugma sa tanan niini nga H+. Kung kulang, naa pa gihapoy mahabilin nga asido.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The neutron was discovered in the year 1932!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: develop a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model that identifies tiny particles as atoms
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a single historical fact (neutron discovered in 1932) that could be used in a timeline of the atomic model, but it does not itself develop a timeline or explain how the neutron discovery contributed to the current Atomic Model. It is useful background rather than direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
When was the neutron finally discovered?

The neutron was discovered in the year 1932! It took scientists a long time to find this neutral particle.
copy.tl:
Kailan natuklas ang neutron?

Natuklas ang neutron noong taong 1932! Matagal na pinag-aralan ng mga siyentipiko bago nila nahanap ang walang kargang particle na ito.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskubre ang neutron?

Ang neutron nadiskubre niadtong tuig 1932! Dugay nga gitudlo sa mga siyentipiko sa dili pa nila makaplagan kini nga walay karga nga particle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fire is very dangerous!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card warns about fire danger but does not explain that changes in materials (e.g., burning household materials) can be harmful to living and non-living things. It lacks the instructional content about material changes and their harmful effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: kids should never play with matches or fire without an adult right nearby
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a fire-safety rule but does not demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restricting burning of waste or handling reactive materials carefully. It does not address material changes or minimization strategies.

copy.en: Fire is very dangerous! That's why kids should never play with matches or fire without an adult right nearby.
copy.tl: Delikado ang apoy! Kaya hindi dapat naglalaro ng posporo o apoy ang mga bata nang walang kasamang matanda.
copy.bis: Delikado ang kalayo! Busa dili angay magdula ang mga bata og posporo o kalayo nga walay kauban nga hamtong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the letter a stands for acceleration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies the symbol 'a' as acceleration. It does not investigate the relationship among force, acceleration, and mass, which is the core action of G9-F-3. Knowing what 'a' means is background knowledge for that investigation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the letter a stands for acceleration
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, and that acceleration of an object is its rate of change of velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card merely states that 'a' represents acceleration. It does not identify that forces cause objects to accelerate, nor does it define acceleration as the rate of change of velocity, which are the required concepts of G8-F-1. The card shares vocabulary but provides no direct instructional support.

copy.en: In the equation F=ma, the letter a stands for acceleration!
copy.tl: Sa F=ma, ang a ay nangangahulugang asintada o acceleration!
copy.bis: Sa F=ma, ang a nagpasabot og acceleration (asintada)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Isaac Newton was an English scientist and mathematician
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Isaac Newton as a famous foreign scientist but does not mention any invention or contribution, which is a required part of the competency. It only provides his nationality, so it does not directly support the skill of identifying a scientist and their invention(s).

copy.en:
Where was the famous scientist Isaac Newton from?

Isaac Newton was an English scientist and mathematician who changed how we see the world!
copy.tl:
Saan nanggaling ang sikat na siyentipikong si Isaac Newton?

Si Isaac Newton ay isang English na siyentipiko at matematiko na nagbago sa ating pananaw sa mundo!
copy.bis:
Hain gikan ang bantog nga siyentista nga si Isaac Newton?

Si Isaac Newton usa ka English nga siyentista ug matematiko nga nagbag-o sa atong panlantaw sa kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientist Isaac Newton gave the name "spectrum" to the band of seven colors of light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a historical fact about who named the band of colors 'spectrum'. It does not explore or describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations, which are the actions required by the competency. The spectrum is a light-related concept, but the card provides no instructional support for the competency's skills.

copy.en: The scientist Isaac Newton gave the name "spectrum" to the band of seven colors of light!
copy.tl: Si Isaac Newton ang nagbigay ng terminong "spectrum" sa hanay ng pitong kulay ng liwanag!
copy.bis: Si Isaac Newton ang naghatag sa pulong nga "spectrum" sa han-ay sa pito ka kolor sa kahayag!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is one of the biggest sources of nickel, a special metal we use to make batteries!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions nickel as a metal used for batteries, but it does not identify properties of metals or describe uses of metals used by the local community (e.g., iron, gold, silver, copper). It only states a single fact about nickel's use in batteries, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Did you know where a lot of the world's battery metal comes from?

The Philippines is one of the biggest sources of nickel, a special metal we use to make batteries!
copy.tl:
Alam mo ba kung saan galing ang maraming metal para sa mga baterya sa mundo?

Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa pinakamalaking pinagkukunan ng nickel, isang metal na ginagamit natin sa mga baterya!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo kung diin naggikan ang daghang metal para sa mga baterya sa kalibutan?

Ang Pilipinas usa sa pinakadakong tinubdan sa nickel, usa ka metal nga gigamit nato sa paghimo og mga baterya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A roof made of nipa leaves helps keep a house cool
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions nipa leaves as a material but does not describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The cooling effect is a functional/thermal property, not one of the listed physical properties, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helps keep a house cool, even on the hottest days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies protection from heat but does not describe any safety measures people can use to avoid harmful effects of the Sun's light. It is about a building material's effect, not about personal safety measures.

copy.en: A roof made of nipa leaves helps keep a house cool, even on the hottest days!
copy.tl: Ang bubong na gawa sa dahon ng nipa ay tumutulong panatilihing malamig ang loob ng bahay kahit sa init!
copy.bis: Ang atop nga hinimo sa dahon sa nipa makatabang nga magpabilin nga bugnaw ang sulod sa balay bisan sa init!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thatched roofs are woven from dried nipa palm leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a traditional roofing material and its water-shedding property, but does not identify a science invention or explain its impact on everyday life as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a palm that grows in salty water near the coast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the nipa palm's habitat (salty water near the coast) and its use for roofing, but does not explain how the plant has adapted to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. The water-shedding property is about the roof, not a plant adaptation.

copy.en: Thatched roofs are woven from dried nipa palm leaves — a palm that grows in salty water near the coast — and they shed rain really well!
copy.tl: Ang bubong na pawid ay gawa sa pinatuyong dahon ng nipa — isang palmang tumutubo sa maalat na tubig malapit sa dagat — at mahusay itong nagtatanggal ng ulan!
copy.bis: Ang atop nga pawid hinimo sa pinauga nga dahon sa nipa — palma nga motubo sa parat nga tubig duol sa baybayon — ug maayo kaayo ni kasalo sa ulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the nitrogen cycle, the same nitrogen is used and returned to nature over and over again, so it's never used up.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using flow charts and labeled diagrams explain the role of plants and animals in the cycles of nature, such as the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the nitrogen cycle, which is a cycle of nature, but the competency specifically requires flow charts and labeled diagrams to explain the role of plants and animals in the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles. The card uses no flow chart or labeled diagram, and nitrogen is not one of the named cycles. It shares the broad topic of natural cycles but does not directly support the required skill or content.

copy.en:
Why doesn't nitrogen ever run out?

In the nitrogen cycle, the same nitrogen is used and returned to nature over and over again, so it's never used up.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi nauubos ang nitrogen?

Sa siklo ng nitrogen, ang parehong nitrogen ay ginagamit at ibinabalik nang paulit-ulit, kaya hindi ito nauubos.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili mahurot ang nitroheno?

Sa siklo sa nitroheno, ang samang nitroheno gigamit ug giuli balik-balik, mao nga dili kini mahurot.
